newsitem.title: USA: Trade chiefs move to settle info technology issue.
newsitem.headline: Trade chiefs move to settle info technology issue.

text.p: Trade ministers from the United States, Japan, European Union and Canada said on Friday they were making progress in trying to resolve differences over an agreement to eliminate tariffs on a wide range of information technologies.

Canadian Trade Minister Arthur Eggleton told reporters following a day-long meeting of the Quadrilateral (Quad) trade ministers that "there is a good chance" the United States and European Union could resolve differences over the information technology agreement (ITA) by the time the trade chiefs end their meeting on Saturday.
"They are making progress," Eggleton told reporters.
The agreement would eliminate tariffs by 2000 on a range of electronic products including computers, chips, software, fax machines, modems and other telecommunications equipment.

EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan has said the main stumbling block is the U.S.-Japan semiconductor alliance. EU officials are concerned European firms will be discriminated against if the wider four-party trade agreement fails to get off the ground.

Officials were planning to work well into Friday night to try to settle differences and reach consensus among the four trading giants in an effort to launch a global agreement at the first meeting of World Trade Organisation ministers in December in Singapore.
U.S. trade officials have said there would be little chance of the ITA being agreed to in December if Quad members were unable to agree among themselves.

"I think it is clear that all countries want to move forward on the ITA, and realise that this window of time represents an important opportunity," said one U.S. official. "I think there is a lot of good faith in trying to find a solution to the problems that up to now have prevented us from moving forward on that."
The World Trade Organisation agenda dominated discussions during Friday's meeting, a U.S. official said.

The four trade ministers also discussed a global agreement to open telecommunications markets and decided the Quad needed to provide leadership on the issue in order to complete negotiations by a February 15 deadline, a U.S. official said.
